Canada. The world's second-largest country by area, occupying the northern portion of the North American continent from the Atlantic to the Pacific and northward to the Arctic Ocean. Originally inhabited by Indigenous peoples for millennia, Canada was colonized by French and British powers, eventually achieving independence within the British Commonwealth and developing into a prosperous, stable democracy.

Canada spans six time zones and encompasses an enormous variety of geography: the Rocky Mountains in the west, vast prairies in the center, the Canadian Shield, an ancient mineral-rich bedrock, in the north and east, and fertile lowlands in the south. Hudson Bay, the world's second-largest bay, dominates Canada's north-central geography. It was the center of the fur trade and remains ecologically significant as a subarctic marine ecosystem. Canada's southern border with the United States is the world's longest international boundary, approximately eight thousand nine hundred kilometers. The two nations share the Great Lakes and major river systems.

Indigenous peoples inhabited Canada for at least fifteen thousand years before European contact. Hundreds of distinct nations, cultures, and languages existed. Colonization by French and British powers devastated Indigenous populations through disease, warfare, and displacement. New France, established by French explorers in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, centered on the St. Lawrence River valley. It was conquered by Britain in the French and Indian War from seventeen fifty-four to seventeen sixty-three, and France ceded all North American territories to Britain. L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland is archaeological evidence of Norse Viking settlement around one thousand CE—the earliest confirmed pre-Columbian European presence in North America.

Canada achieved Confederation in eighteen sixty-seven as a self-governing dominion within the British Empire. It gradually acquired full sovereignty, completed in nineteen eighty-two with the patriation of its constitution. Modern Canada is a multicultural, bilingual nation with English and French as official languages. It has strong traditions of democracy, rule of law, and social welfare, and remains a Commonwealth realm with the British monarch as head of state.
